title: NaN breadcrumbs / hypothesis log — quant transition
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent NaNs seen when switching model from bf16 to int8 quantized runtime in the nightly A/B test. Failures sporadic: ~1/200 requests on long-context prompts (>=1024).
- bf16 and fp32 runs are stable (no NaNs) but int8 and fp8 variants show token-level NaNs in logits that then propagate into softmax -> sampling -> catastrophic output.

Environment:
- commit: 9f3d7a2 (serving-runtime: quant/kv-fix branch)
- container: rwinf/runner:prod-20240121
- GPU: A100-SXM4 80GB, driver 535.xx, cuda 12.1
- inference stack: pytorch-nightly 2.2.0.dev, custom kernels + Triton kernels for attention
- model: open-llm/titan-3b-like (transformer-decoder), layernorm pre-attn, rotary embeddings, cached KV enabled

Repro (fast local):
1) ./tools/run_inference.py --model titan-small --mode int8 --calib-data samples/calib-2k.jsonl --batch 1 --seq-len 1536 --beam 1
   -> observed NaN at token 42 consistently when using this prompt set (subset A).
2) same command with --mode bf16 -> no NaN, output OK but perplexity worse by ~0.6.
3) run with --int8-perchannel True -> still NaN. --int8-symmetric False/True toggles didn't change outcome.

Raw snippets (stdout/stderr):
- WARNING: attention_kv_cache: hole detected at layer 12, idx 2048
- RuntimeError: NaN detected in logits at softmax input (layer 23, head 5, token 42)
- backtrace: at aten::softmax -> serving_runtime::kernels::stable_softmax (qbuf.cc:201) -> runtime_main.cc:541
- kernel debug: max(abs(input)) = 1.8e38, found inf/NaN after adding bias folding term

Commands tried (and notes):
- baseline: --mode bf16 (ok)
- quantize with per-channel scales: --mode int8 --calib-perchannel True (still NaN)
- reduce seq len: --seq-len 512 (NaN disappears) => suggests accumulation/overflow with long context
- disable kv cache: --kv-cache False (NaN disappears) => implicates KV cache / rotary interaction
- clamp attention scores: added soft-clamp to attention logits at 1e2 (quick patch) -> reduced NaN frequency but not eliminated
- switch embedding dtype to fp16 (workspace) -> no change
- set rounding_mode stochastic -> marginal improvement (NaNs less frequent)
- use different calibration dataset (calib-other.jsonl with shorter tails) -> NaNs less frequent

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization range calibration misses rare activation outliers produced only with long-context + kv-cache; those outliers then get saturated/overflowed when converted to int8, producing extremely large values after dequant+matmul that blow up softmax. Evidence: disappears when seq-len reduced and when using different calib set.
2) KV cache concatenation bug where offsets computed with 32-bit index but stored in 16-bit intermediates -> misaligned memory reads producing garbage (NaN) sporadically. Evidence: warning about hole detected; toggling kv-cache fixed in some runs.
3) Rotary embedding math interaction with quantized inplace ops leads to precision loss accumulating across past tokens (especially with per-tensor quant). Evidence: quantized per-channel didn't fix; rotary present in failing model.
4) Attention kernel numeric instability with fused matmul+softmax in int8 path — kernel implementation uses an approximate rescale that under/overflows for certain input distributions. Evidence: kernel debug logs show massive max(abs(input)) in failing cases.

Immediate experiments to run (actionable checklist):
- [ ] Re-run failing prompt with memory-checker + ASAN-like memguard to catch misaligned reads (to test hypothesis 2).
- [ ] Add a simple pre-softmax clamp (e.g., clamp(x, -30, 30)) in int8 path to see if NaNs become stable numerics — quick diagnostic (not a permanent fix).
- [ ] Recompute calibration stats using the actual long-context prompt set (simulate streaming past tokens) and re-quantize weights/scales — see if calibration shift fixes it.
- [ ] Instrument KV write/read offsets to log shapes and offsets on edge-case runs.
- [ ] Try disabling rotary (compile variant without rotary) to test hypothesis 3.
- [ ] Run with higher internal accumulation dtype (simulate int32 accumulation to float) in matmul to see if overflow originates from accumulation width.

Notes on calibration and quant params I suspect matter:
- per-channel vs per-tensor scale: per-channel should help, but if activation outliers come from positional accumulation (across tokens) per-channel may not capture temporal spikes.
- asymmetric quantization tends to shift distributions; zero_point drift can amplify small negative logits into large post-dequant values.
- clipping thresholds used during calibration (99.9th percentile vs max) — using max is sensitive to single outliers, but percentiles can miss extreme, rare spikes.

Small experiment logs (timestamps):
- 2024-02-12 09:14: ran baseline bf16/ok
- 2024-02-12 10:02: int8 with calib-2k -> NaN token 42 (repeatable)
- 2024-02-13 15:24: int8 + disable-kv -> PASS
- 2024-02-14 11:03: int8 + clamp logits (|x|<100) -> NaN rate from 0.5% -> 0.1%
- 2024-02-18 16:45: int8 + stochastic rounding -> NaN rate ~0.08%

Why bf16 'fixes' but degrades quality:
- bf16 preserves enough dynamic range per activation so no catastrophic overflow; however, scaling from bf16 to fp32 for scoring may add noise and quantization noise from other parts still present — net effect: stable numerics but slightly worse perplexity compared to full-precision tuned int8 path.

Longer-term remediation ideas:
- Improve calibration pipeline: include streaming long-context distributions, add 'stress' examples to ensure tails covered.
- Add defensive clamping/overflow guards in attention kernels (and possibly log caches of extreme values for telemetry).
- Revisit KV-cache layout and bounds checks; add debug-only checksum on KV writes to detect miswrites.
- Introduce a hybrid runtime that uses bf16 for attention accumulators and int8 for matmul weights to preserve dynamic range where needed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there other models using rotary + kv-cache + int8 that are stable? (compare infra telemetry)
- Does Triton kernel version affect this? Need to test older/newer triton kernels (benchmarks pending).
- Should we add a runtime switch to automatically escalate to bf16 on NaN detection (self-healing fallback)? Pros: uptime; Cons: perf variance.

Quick links to related artifacts:
- GH PR: serving-runtime/pull/1423 (kv cache bounds patches)
- JIRA INF-9876: "Intermittent NaNs on quantized paths"
- Confluence page: Model-Quantization-Playbook (calibration heuristics)

Final note (for my future self):
- Start with the simplest repro that reliably shows NaN (the prompt set A + int8 on A100 coaxed by --seq-len 1536). Lock exact seed and input. If a deterministic repro exists, prioritize binary search over commits to find the regression.

-- Asha
